en: Taal Volcano in Batangas features a massive main crater lake that surrounds Volcano Island, which itself contains a smaller crater lake.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an underground river that flows directly into the sea, making it subject to ocean tides.
Mount Pulag, the highest peak in Luzon, is famous for its breathtaking sea of clouds that forms above 2,200 meters.
Mount Hamiguitan in Davao Oriental is the only place in the world where the rare Nepenthes hamiguitanensis pitcher plant naturally grows.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
During the amihan or northeast monsoon, cool and dry winds from Asia bring pleasant, dry weather to the Philippines.
The Verde Island Passage in Batangas is scientifically recognized as the center of the world's marine shorefish biodiversity.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago using hand tools.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has eyes that are as large as its entire brain to help it see at night.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in Zambales was the second-largest of the 20th century and temporarily cooled global temperatures.
The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands, but only about 2,000 of them are officially inhabited.
Callao Cave in Cagayan features a massive limestone chamber that acts as a natural chapel illuminated by a hole in the ceiling.
